source.title: Spectral Analysis of Latent Representations
source.authors: Justin C. Shenk; Mats L. Richter; Anders Arpteg; Mikael Huss

record.tranche_reason: The paper varies network width and measures test performance, bearing on whether wider networks continue to generalize. It does not test random-label memorization, compare convolutional with fully connected models, or measure magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: The study reports width and depth sweeps and relates layer saturation to predictive performance. It does not train on random labels or directly compare training and test error gaps as specified by most versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation saturation and predictive performance across network sizes. It does not establish the zero-training-error width threshold needed to test V2's claim about widening beyond interpolation, and it tests none of the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that layer-wise and average saturation relate to performance, dataset difficulty and network structure, and that saturation patterns can help identify under- or overparameterization.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures saturation while varying width and depth; it does not use the original claim's interpolation-threshold setup or test-error-gap comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset complexity, network depth, and filter-stack width influence saturation and its relationship with performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Wider fully connected networks generally attain better test accuracy and lower representation saturation in the tested width range, but interpolation is not established.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing hidden-layer width can improve held-out accuracy under a fixed 20-epoch training budget on CIFAR10 and its cat-versus-dog subset.

fits_no_version.finding: Representation saturation relates to predictive performance, network size and problem complexity; layer-wise patterns can indicate insufficient or excess capacity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The dimensionality of learned representations relative to layer width can inform architecture assessment.

record.problems: The text presents the relevant trends mainly in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates; experiments use 20 epochs regardless of dataset, network and architecture.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only individual width, depth and filter-size values are not transcribed; the text provides aggregate trend statements instead.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Whether test error continues falling as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error. The fixed 20-epoch sweeps do not establish interpolation or training to convergence.
Comparative generalization of convolutional and fully connected networks, including local connectivity and initialization interventions.
Adaptive-versus-SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions; all experiments use Adam.
Batch-size effects and compensating recipes; batch size is fixed at 128.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Memorization-based example removal versus random removal and subsequent test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed V2 limits_scope verdict: failure to establish the interpolation condition is an untested component, not evidence that V2 needs qualification. Numerical points omitted from the figures are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Zero training error/interpolation threshold; MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity interventions.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation of large-batch recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on test error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples and the resulting change in test accuracy.

rows.subject: three-layer fully connected neural networks
rows.size_stated: Hidden layer of 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128 units; input layer 128 units; softmax layer with 10 or 2 units.
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-layer width on CIFAR10 and cat-vs-dog; compared saturation with test performance.
rows.value: The text states that higher-parameterized networks generally achieve better performance and lower saturation; lower-saturation models tend to perform better until overfitting occurs.
rows.note: The stated trend bears on width and test performance, but the study does not establish zero training error or a threshold beyond which widening lowers test error. Figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The reported tendency toward better test accuracy with greater width is valid, but no zero-training-error threshold or post-threshold comparison is established. It therefore cannot show either a full or partial V2 effect. Figure 5 includes both datasets; Figure 8 concerns CIFAR10.

rows.subject: VGG11, VGG13, VGG16 and VGG19 architectures
rows.size_stated: Depths 11, 13, 16 and 19 layers; five filter widths: full, half, quarter, eighth or sixteenth of original filters.
rows.operation_detail: Varied depth and filter width and measured average saturation and classification performance.
rows.value: The text states that lower average saturation generally corresponds to higher performance; depth and filter-stack size influence saturation, and performance declines more rapidly for the more complex problem after roughly 45% saturation.
rows.note: This is a convolutional architecture sweep and a saturation-performance finding; it does not compare against fully connected networks or isolate the claim versions.
rows.check: The saturation-performance association does not measure any version's specified effect. The convolutional sweep establishes neither post-interpolation widening nor a controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Fully connected width sweep on CIFAR10 and cat-vs-dog
reader_labels.reason: The authors report generally better performance for higher-parameterized networks, but do not show that widening beyond zero training error continues lowering test error (R1).
